overview.headline: 2026 tax inflation adjustments raise deductions, brackets and credits

keyPoints.point: Students learn the 2026 standard deduction amounts differ by filing status and increase from 2025.
keyPoints.quote: For tax year 2026, the standard deduction increases to $32,200 for married couples filing jointly.

keyPoints.point: Students learn the top 2026 individual rate remains 37 percent above income thresholds that vary by filing status.
keyPoints.quote: For tax year 2026, the top tax rate remains 37% for individual single taxpayers with incomes greater than $640,600

keyPoints.point: Students learn estates of decedents dying during 2026 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,000,000.
keyPoints.quote: Estates of decedents who die during 2026 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,000,000

keyPoints.point: Students learn the maximum 2026 Earned Income Tax Credit for three or more children is $8,231.
keyPoints.quote: The tax year 2026 maximum Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) amount is $8,231

keyTerms.gloss: Amount that reduces taxable income based on filing status without itemizing deductions.
keyTerms.quote: For tax year 2026, the standard deduction increases to $32,200 for married couples filing jointly.

keyTerms.gloss: Income thresholds where different tax rates apply to single and joint filers.
keyTerms.quote: Marginal Rates: For tax year 2026, the top tax rate remains 37% for individual single taxpayers

keyTerms.gloss: Minimum tax exemption that phases out above income limits for unmarried filers.
keyTerms.quote: Alternative Minimum Tax Exemption Amounts. For tax year 2026, the exemption amount for unmarried individuals is $90,100

keyTerms.gloss: Refundable credit whose maximum amount rises with number of qualifying children.
keyTerms.quote: The tax year 2026 maximum Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) amount is $8,231
